name: Toggl
summary: Time tracking and capacity planning for freelancers, consultants and agencies, with budgets, rates and profitability per project. Relaunched from Toggl Track to Toggl in 2026.
best_for: freelancers, consultants and agencies that bill by the hour and want frictionless tracking with budgets, rates and profitability per project
skip_if: you need surveillance-style monitoring (screenshots, activity scoring — deliberately not Toggl's philosophy), or free-tier tracking already covers you
honest_knock: Toggl's honesty problem is the good kind: the free tier is so capable that many teams never need to pay — the paid line is drawn exactly at 'do you bill clients' (budgets, rates, profitability). If you do, Starter earns itself fast; if you track time for personal discipline, resist the upgrade. Time tracking's real cost everywhere is adoption: the tool is frictionless, but the habit still has to be built. Two newer cost lines are easy to miss: leave approvals and accruals sit in the $2 Time Off Pro add-on rather than in any plan, and capacity planning beyond the current month is the Capacity Management add-on at $5 to $6 per user, so a team buying Premium for planning should price both.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month billed annually, or $12 monthly
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-09-09 and again 2026-10-01 on toggl.com/track/pricing, which now redirects to toggl.com/pricing) Free is $0 and the page calls it free forever; the pricing FAQ read 22 October 2026 sets its limit at up to 3 users. Starter is $9 per user a month billed annually and $12 monthly; Premium is $16 annually and $24 monthly; Enterprise is quoted. The introductory $14 Premium rate renewing at $18 that we recorded in August is gone — Premium now carries one annual price. The billing toggle advertises 'Annual (Save 33.3%)' and '4 months free', which holds exactly for Premium but not for Starter, where $12 to $9 is 25%. Trial is 30 days; Enterprise adds volume discounts on annual and multiple workspaces under one organisation. Re-read on 22 October 2026 with the same four plans and figures. What is new is the product around them: the pricing page now sells one Toggl that combines time tracking with project planning and capacity management, and notes that Toggl Track and Toggl Plan remain available and supported for existing users. Two paid add-ons sit on top of the paid plans: Time Off Pro at $2 per user a month (approval workflows, accrual balances, custom leave policies) and Capacity Management at $5 per user a month billed annually or $6 monthly (capacity beyond the current month, team roll-ups, draft projects, forecasting).

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 28 October 2026 on the free trial: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We logged three time entries with known durations, set a billable rate, exported the reports, tried to import one export again and opened the upgrade without paying.
findings: Signing up at track.toggl.com put us in the new Toggl Focus app. After three onboarding screens a dialog said 'The whole product is unlocked for 31 days' and 'No credit card needed'; the pricing page we read on 25 October says a 30-day trial. The upgrade screen gave the trial end as November 28.

Our three entries (a 2m 18s timer, 15:00 and 1:30 by hand) added up to exactly 18m 48s in the report breakdown. The summary tiles rounded that to 19m, while the day header in the timer list showed 18m.

A project with a $60 hourly rate turned the 15-minute entry into $15.00 and 79.79% billable, both correct. Billable rates are one of eight features the project view labels as unlocked by the Premium trial.

The Time logs CSV kept all three entries to the second, with project, client and amount on the right row. The Summary CSV put all 0:18:48 under the one project, although only 15 minutes belonged to it. Every export format (PDF, CSV, XLSX) carries a paid-feature star.

Importing our own Time logs export again did not work as is: the importer asked for a duration column, could not use the combined start-and-stop column, and read the export's '-' placeholders as names, so all three entries would have been skipped. We stopped before importing; there is no ID column to update by.

Monthly prices in the app were $12 for Starter and $24 for Premium per license ($9 and $16 a month billed yearly). Choosing Premium warned that 'your current trial will finish immediately', so we stopped there. After the trial the app says you can 'keep going free — no charge', and the Free plan allows up to 5 members.
The invite dialog offers Workspace admin, Manager, Member, Time tracker and Guest, with no role preselected. Billing lists 'Change plan' and 'Cancel trial' in the plan menu.
not_tested: The final checkout with tax (choosing a plan ends the trial straight away)
Export and members on the Free plan after the trial ends
Completing a re-import (we stopped at the preview)
The calendar connection, Toggl AI and the mobile and desktop apps
sessions.note: Findings as written up after the session; no pass/fail per task was scored.
